name: Simple Notice Board – Easy Announcements and Notices
author: Inu Etc

sections.description:
Simple Notice Board is a lightweight and easy-to-use WordPress plugin that lets you display important notices, announcements, or updates anywhere on your website with a simple shortcode. Perfect for schools, colleges, organizations, businesses, and communities that need a quick way to publish and share updates with visitors.
The plugin is designed to be clean, minimal, and distraction-free — ensuring your visitors see your notices clearly.

Features

  • Add, Edit, or Delete Notices Easily – Manage all your notices directly from the WordPress dashboard.
  • Simple & Clean Design – Frontend notice board displays in a clear, scrollable list.
  • Automatic Refresh – Notices update automatically when you add or edit them.
  • Shortcode Support – Display your notice board anywhere using: [notice_board]
  • Responsive – Works smoothly across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

Use Cases

  • School/College notice boards
  • Career & Recruitment updates
  • Corporate announcements
  • Event updates
  • Community or non-profit bulletin boards
  • Temporary messages or alerts for visitors

Shortcode

To display the notice board anywhere on your site: [notice_board]

Technical Details

  • Requires WordPress 5.0 or higher
  • Lightweight and performance-friendly
  • No bloated options — simple and focused

👉 Keep your visitors updated with Simple Notice Board — the fastest way to share important news and announcements on your WordPress site.

sections.installation:
1. Download the plugin .zip file and upload it via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin in your WordPress admin panel.
    Or, simply search for “Simple Notice Board” in the WordPress Plugin Directory from your WordPress dashboard and install it directly.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Add notices under Notices in your dashboard.
  4. Place the shortcode [notice_board] anywhere on your site (page, post, or widget) to display the notice board.
sections.faq:
How do I display the notices?

Use the shortcode [notice_board] in your posts, pages, or widgets.
